Almeida Benalcazar, E., Noorman, H., Maciel Filho, R. and Posada, J.A. (2022). Decarbonizing ethanol production via gas fermentation: Impact of the CO/H2/CO2 mix source on greenhouse gas emissions and production costs. Computers and Chemical Engineering 159, 107670. doi:10.1016/j.compchemeng.2022.107670

Locator: printed journal page (pages 1-14 of article 107670 are numbered in the footer). Gas-fermentation ethanol model study (BOF steel off-gas, biomass syngas, H2/CO2) with Monte Carlo sensitivity and NSGA-II optimization. Loaded: optimized ethanol production costs (EPC, 2019 EUR/L ethanol) at the 'ideal' and 'realistic' Pareto optimum for the three gas sources and the 220 kt/y throughput. NOT loaded: capex (the paper gives only unit purchase costs; whole-plant CAPEX = 6.8 x purchase cost is in the supplementary Tables SI6, not held), energy use per litre (only in Figs SI9 and charts, not printed), emissions (life-cycle GWP incl. product combustion, not scope 1); chart-only values omitted. EPC includes gas feedstock cost and so is not a fermenter-only cost. Table 3 purchase-cost years are the original cost years, converted to 2019 EUR by the authors. Median distributions (Fig. 3) are charts only.
